title: Credit Administration Standard — Number of Farm Real Estate Loans a Member May Hold
content:
**Standard.** A member may hold any number of Farm Real Estate Loans; there is no per-member maximum. Each purchase or refinance of a distinct set of parcels is its own loan, with its own mortgage, its own rate product and its own schedule. How loans held together are tested is set by the combined loan-to-value test for Farm Real Estate Loans.

## The standard restated

| Question the standard answers | Answer |
|---|---|
| Is there a limit on how many farm real estate loans one member holds? | No — no per-member maximum is set. |
| What makes a separate loan? | Each purchase or refinance of a distinct set of parcels. |
| What does each loan carry of its own? | Its own mortgage, its own FarmLand rate product and its own installment schedule. |
| How are several loans of one member looked at together? | Through the combined loan-to-value test. |

**Illustration (hypothetical).** A member who bought a quarter section of dryland cropland on one loan and later refinanced a separate pasture tract holds two Farm Real Estate Loans: each has its own mortgage on its own parcels, and each may be on a different FarmLand product — for instance one on the FarmLand 5-Year Adjustable Mortgage and the other on the FarmLand 15-Year Fixed Mortgage — with its own schedule.
